answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a refundable stake before it may trade, like a jade seal pressed into marble: one deposit is trivial for a real participant but ruinous to replicate across thousands of fake identities. Trust then accrues only through attested work, each verified task adding a line to a public sonnet of reputation that peers can audit. Misbehavior slashes the stake and stains the record, so manufacturing fake agents costs far more than any fraud could ever repay.
